title: KDP Paperback Cover Requirements: The Full Checklist (2026) | Legenddary's SparkPrep
h1: KDP paperback cover requirements: the full checklist
description: Every Amazon KDP paperback cover rule in plain English: one PDF, 0.125" bleed, the cover size formula, spine width by paper, 300 DPI, spine text over 79 pages, and the mistakes that get covers rejected.
lead: KDP wants your paperback cover as one file that wraps around the whole book. Get a few numbers right and it goes through. Get one wrong and it comes back. Here is every rule, from KDP's own help pages, in plain English.

answer.q: What are the KDP paperback cover requirements?
answer.a: KDP wants one PDF with the back, spine and front together, 0.125" bleed on every side, and images at 300 DPI or more. Cover width is bleed + back + spine + front + bleed. Keep text at least 0.125" inside the trim, and only put words on the spine if the book has more than 79 pages.

body:
1. One file, three parts

A KDP paperback cover is a single PDF: back cover on the left, spine in the middle, front cover on the right, as one continuous image. Not three files, and not just the front.

2. The size: use this formula

  • Width = 0.125" bleed + back cover width + spine width + front cover width + 0.125" bleed
  • Height = 0.125" bleed + trim height + 0.125" bleed

Example: a 6" x 9" book with 200 pages on white paper has a 0.451" spine, so the cover is 12.701" x 9.25". Work out yours with the free KDP cover calculator or see every size on book cover dimensions.

3. The spine depends on your paper

PaperSpine = page count x200 pages
White (black ink)0.002252"0.451"
Cream (black ink)0.0025"0.5"
Standard color0.002252"0.451"
Premium color0.002347"0.469"

Change your page count or paper and the spine changes, so the whole cover changes. That's the most common reason a cover that "used to fit" gets rejected. More on this in white vs cream paper.

4. Bleed: color all the way past the edge

Backgrounds and pictures must run 0.125" past the trim line on every side. That strip is cut off. If your background stops at the trim, you can get a thin white line on the edge of the printed book. See what bleed is.

5. Keep words away from the edges

  • Text on the front and back: at least 0.125" inside the trim. KDP's guidelines also say anything you don't want cut off should be 0.25" from the outside edge, so 0.25" is the safer number.
  • No front or back text running onto the spine.
  • Text at least 7 points, and a different enough color from the background to read.

6. Spine text: only on books over 79 pages

KDP only prints spine text on books with more than 79 pages. A thinner book with spine text gets rejected. Keep spine words at least 0.0625" from each side of the spine, because the fold can shift a little.

7. Pictures and color

  • At least 300 DPI at the size they print. Check yours with the free DPI checker.
  • KDP asks for images in CMYK, one color space, no spot colors. See RGB vs CMYK.
  • Flatten layers and transparency, and embed every font.

8. Leave room for the barcode

You can add your own barcode, or leave the bottom of the back cover clear and KDP adds one. Don't put words or faces where it will go. See barcode placement.

9. Take these out before you upload

  • Crop marks, trim marks and color bars
  • Template guide lines and placeholder text
  • Watermarks or "made with" logos
  • Passwords or file locks
  • Emoji or odd symbols in the file name

KDP lists each of these as a reason files fail. The title on your cover must also match the title you typed in KDP exactly.

All rules from KDP's Create a Paperback Cover and Paperback Submission Guidelines pages, checked November 26, 2026. KDP's limit is 650 MB per cover file; it recommends 40 MB or less.

faq.q: What file type does KDP want for a paperback cover?
faq.a: One PDF with the back cover, spine and front cover together as a single image. KDP's Cover Creator also takes JPG, PNG or GIF, but an uploaded cover must be a PDF.

faq.q: How much bleed does a KDP cover need?
faq.a: 0.125 inch on every side. Backgrounds and pictures should run 0.125 inch past the trim line so no white edge shows after cutting.

faq.q: Can I put text on the spine of a thin book?
faq.a: Only if the book has more than 79 pages. KDP doesn't print spine text on thinner books and rejects covers that have it.
